title: Fake "Claude Opus 5 Free Desktop" app spreads RevStealer infostealer, researchers say
date_note: GBHackers and Cyber Security News (both 23 Nov) report the campaign; Cyberint's report is dated 18 October per Cyber Security News. Neither page read gives a later disclosure day.
summary: Cyberint researchers, as relayed by GBHackers and Cyber Security News, describe a fake "Claude Opus 5 Free Desktop" app that installs RevStealer, a Windows infostealer. Cyber Security News says Cyberint did not attribute it to a named threat actor. GBHackers says there is no sign Anthropic was compromised, and that Morphisec confirmed it looks for 12 password managers and more than 50 crypto wallets.
plain: A fake Claude desktop app installs password- and crypto-wallet-stealing malware. Researchers say Anthropic itself was not compromised.
exec: Fake AI-app lure can steal saved passwords and crypto wallets from Windows users who run it.
action: GBHackers advises downloading Claude only from claude.com/download, and if the fake app was run, treating the system as compromised and rotating passwords from a clean device.
impact: Credential and crypto-wallet theft on Windows PCs that run the fake app.

evidence.quote: Morphisec confirmed it looks for 12 password managers and more than 50 crypto wallets.

validation.note: GBHackers and Cyber Security News both relay Cyberint's research, so they are not independent; the Cyberint and Morphisec originals were not read.
